target.title: fix(imessage): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in the RPC client child
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iMessage RPC client spawns a long-lived `imsg` helper child process. When that child dies, its stdio streams can emit an asynchronous `error` event (for example `EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET` when writing to or reading from a dead pipe). On a raw Node stream, an unhandled `'error'` event is re-thrown and surfaces as an `uncaughtException`, which takes down the whole gateway process.

This exact crash class was reported and fixed for **stdin** in #75438 (`IMessageRpcClient.request() does not handle async stdin write errors → uncaughtException → gateway crash`). The fix added a `child.stdin.on("error", …)` listener, but the sibling `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` streams on the same child were left unguarded — so a dead-child error arriving on stdout or stderr still crashes the gateway.

This mirrors the child-process stream-error hardening recently merged across the runtime (e.g. #100849 node-host `runCommand`, #100861 auto-reply `scpFile`), applied to the iMessage channel's own helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

`start()` already routes `child.on("error")` and `child.stdin.on("error")` into `failAll(...)`. stdout and stderr belong to the same child and carry the same hazard, so they are routed through the same failure path. The three listeners are collapsed into a small shared `failFromStreamError` helper to keep the behavior identical across streams and avoid drift. No control-flow, framing, or RPC-parsing behavior changes — this only prevents an unhandled stream `'error'` from escaping as an `uncaughtException`.

Scope is intentionally limited to `client.ts` (the long-lived RPC client, the surface named in #75438). The one-shot iMessage CLI spawns in `send.ts` / `actions.runtime.ts` share the pattern and can follow as separate narrow changes.

## User Impact

A misbehaving or killed `imsg` helper (crash, Full Disk Access loss, forced kill, pipe reset) no longer risks crashing the entire gateway via an uncaughtException from a stdout/stderr stream error. In-flight RPC requests reject cleanly with the stream error instead. iMessage users on macOS get a more resilient gateway; there is no config, API, or behavior change for anyone else.

## Evidence

Focused regression test added (`client.test.ts`): spawns the client against a mock child, then emits `'error'` on `stdout`, `stderr`, and `stdin` respectively and asserts (a) the emit does not throw (an unguarded raw stream would throw synchronously — the real crash path) and (b) the in-flight request rejects with the stream error.

- Targeted run (extension-imessage vitest lane): **3/3 pass**.
- Negative control: reverting the two new stdout/stderr listeners makes the stdout and stderr cases fail with `expected [Function] to not throw … 'Error: stdout broke' was thrown` (and stderr likewise), while the stdin case still passes — confirming the test guards the real regression and the fix resolves it.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both files.

Typecheck/lint fan-out and the full changed-gate were not run in this sparse worktree (module-resolution for `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` requires a full checkout); they are left to CI on the exact head SHA. The change adds no new types beyond a local `(err: unknown) => void` helper.
